summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require Infrastructure Australia to give greater consideration to social and community benefits when auditing infrastructure, assessing proposals and preparing national infrastructure priorities.
It would add rural and regional social needs to assessments, require consultation with affected communities, and include current and future users’ needs in advice.
The requirements would apply to activities begun from commencement, the day after Royal Assent, while work already underway would not have to meet them.
changes: Infrastructure plans would consider social benefits and complementary infrastructure needed to maximise those benefits.
Advice on infrastructure matters would have to consider social issues.
Preparing or changing corporate plans would require community consultation.
summary.affected: Infrastructure Australia, affected rural and regional communities and infrastructure users are affected.
